newsitem.title: SPAIN: Talks over Tisa purchase still underway - Telefonica.
newsitem.headline: Talks over Tisa purchase still underway - Telefonica.

text.p: Spain's Telefonica said on Monday that it was still in talks to buy the state's 23.8 percent stake in its international arm Telefonica Internacional SA (Tisa) and that no deal had been closed.
"The operation is still being discussed and there is nothing official yet," a Telefonica spokesman sid.
On Saturday, Spanish daily El Pais said Telefonica had agreed the state would have revenues of 106 billion pesetas for the sale of its direct stake in Tisa.
The remaining 76.2 percent stake of Tisa is already owned by Telefonica.

This price would fall near the middle of the band of 94.8 to 116.5 billion pesetas estimated by Salomon Brothers, but would differ substantially from the 140 billion pesetas initially forecast by the state for the sale of its stake.
The Economy Ministry also said it had no word of an accord.
"The only thing we know is that last Friday, Salomon Brothers handed in its estimate of the value of the state stake in Tisa," an Economy Ministry spokesman said.
In October, Tisa managing director Marcial Portela told Reuters Telefonica could buy the stake before its privatisation.

The Economy Ministry spokesman said no specific date had yet been set for the privatisation of the state's remaining 21.16 percent stake in Telefonica, although the government has said the sale would take place in the first few months of 1997.
Last week, Telefonica said the government would approve the privatisation at the cabinet meeting on December 13.
